1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nd4.name: Ruy Lopez: Bird Variation
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nd4.background: Published in 1843 in Paul Rudolf von Bilguer's Handbuch des Schachspiels and explored by Henry Bird in the late nineteenth century; Bird played it as Black at least 25 times, scoring nine wins, thirteen losses and three draws. No strong master since Bird has adopted it regularly.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nd4 4.Nxd4.strategy: Takes the knight at once: White gives Black no time to profit from the attack on the bishop. Black recaptures with the pawn and gains space on d4 at the cost of doubled pawns and a lag in development.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nd4 4.Nxd4 exd4.strategy: The only sensible recapture. The pawn on d4 cramps White's queenside development and is not easy to dislodge, but Black has doubled pawns and is behind in development.
